commands.name: teamrun.listProjects
commands.description: Prints each project's id, name and folder.

commands.name: teamrun.openFolder
commands.summary: Opens a folder as a project.
commands.description: Opens the folder as a project, or gives the project already open there, and prints its id, name and folder. A folder given as a relative path is read from the current folder, a leading ~ is the home folder, and a folder that isn't there is refused.

commands.name: teamrun.forgetProject
commands.summary: Forgets a project and deletes its chats.
commands.description: Forgets the project and deletes its chats and their messages; the folder's files stay.

commands.name: teamrun.listChats
commands.description: Prints each chat's id, title and teammates, and whether a reply is running, of every project and the chats without one, or of the project given.

options.name: project
options.description: The id of the project whose chats to list.

commands.name: teamrun.newChat
commands.summary: Starts a chat, in a project or in a folder of its own.
commands.description: Starts an empty chat in the project, or without a project in an empty folder of its own, and prints its id and title.

arguments.name: projectId
arguments.description: The id of the project the chat belongs to; a chat without a project when left out.

options.name: title
options.description: The chat's title; by default TeamRun's own.

examples.description: Starts the chat Notes in project 7f3c.
Starts the chat Notes without a project.

arguments.name: title
arguments.description: The new title, the rest of the line.

examples.description: Renames chat c41a to Release notes.

commands.name: teamrun.deleteChat
commands.summary: Deletes a chat and its messages.

commands.name: teamrun.moveChat
commands.summary: Moves a chat to another project.
commands.description: Moves the chat to the project, and prints its id, project and title.

arguments.name: projectId
arguments.description: The id of the project to move it to.

commands.name: teamrun.search
commands.summary: Finds chats by their title or messages.
commands.description: Prints each chat whose title or messages hold the text, ignoring case, the latest active first: its id and title, and where the text is, in the title or in a message, with that message's number and the text around it.

arguments.name: text
arguments.description: The text to find, the rest of the line.

options.name: limit
options.description: How many chats to list at most, from 1 to 100.

examples.description: Lists at most five chats that mention release notes.

commands.name: teamrun.listMessages
commands.description: Prints the chat's latest messages, or those before a sequence number, each with its number, author, status and text. The person's own messages are by User, and a message a teammate sent from another chat names that teammate and chat, such as @Alice in chat "Release" (c41a), or the default teammate (Codex) in chat "Release" (c41a).

options.name: before
options.description: Lists only the messages before this sequence number.

options.name: limit
options.description: How many messages to list at most.

examples.description: Lists the ten messages of chat c41a before message 40.

commands.name: teamrun.send
commands.summary: Sends a message to a chat.
commands.description: Sends the message as the app does, with @mentions naming teammates, and prints the ids of the message and of the replies it started, without waiting for them. When it names no teammate and no kind, the default teammate answers, not the responder chosen in the chat's composer, with the model, effort and provider given here in place of its own. Run from a teammate's process in a chat, it sends as that teammate and chat, and a chat whose reply is running starts it after.

arguments.name: text
arguments.description: The message, the rest of the line, or - alone to read it from standard input.

options.name: teammate
options.description: The teammate who answers, by name.

options.name: kind
options.description: The kind of provider, such as codex or claude, that answers when no teammate is named, in place of the default teammate; give it with --provider, one of that kind's providers.

options.name: model
options.description: The provider's model, at its own default effort unless --effort is given.

options.name: provider
options.description: The id of the provider that answers when no teammate is named. In place of the default teammate's, one of another kind answers with its own model and effort, and one of its kind keeps the default's model and effort only where that provider's models list them.

examples.arguments: c41a @Reviewer please check the release notes
examples.description: Asks the teammate Reviewer in chat c41a.

examples.arguments: c41a --teammate Reviewer Check the release notes
examples.description: Sends the message for the teammate Reviewer to answer.
Sends what standard input holds for the teammate Reviewer to answer.

commands.name: teamrun.rewind
commands.summary: Removes a message and those after it.
commands.description: Removes the chat's message and every message after it, and prints how many it removed and whether the provider's session continues from there or the next reply starts a fresh one. With --restore-files it also puts back the files the removed replies changed, where their checkpoints allow, and says why when it can't.

arguments.name: messageId
arguments.description: The id of the first message to remove.

options.name: restoreFiles
options.description: Puts back the files the removed replies changed.

examples.description: Removes message m7 of chat c41a and those after it, and puts their files back.

commands.name: teamrun.listApprovals
commands.description: Prints each approval's id, status, summary and options.

options.name: pending
options.description: Lists only the approvals that wait for an answer.

examples.description: Lists the approvals chat c41a waits on.

commands.name: teamrun.listProviders
commands.description: Prints each provider's id, kind, name and sign-in status.

commands.name: teamrun.addProvider
commands.summary: Adds a provider with a new profile folder of its own.
commands.description: Adds a provider of the kind, with the label and a new profile folder in TeamRun's data folder, and prints its id, label and kind; it signs in from TeamRun's window. Some kinds take one provider at most.

arguments.name: kind
arguments.description: The kind of provider, such as codex or claude.

commands.name: teamrun.removeProvider
commands.description: Removes the provider and leaves its profile folder as it is; a default teammate that answered with it has no provider until one is chosen.

commands.name: teamrun.listModels
commands.description: Prints each model's id, name and efforts, and which is the provider's default.

commands.name: teamrun.liveCheck
commands.summary: Runs one reply of a provider end to end.
commands.description: Starts a chat without a project, in an empty folder of its own, sends the prompt to the provider at its default model, waits for the reply, deletes the chat and its folder, and prints the reply. It fails when the reply ends other than completed, with the reply's error. A reply that asks for an approval, which only the window answers, is stopped, and the check fails. A chat it can't delete is named, for delete-chat to remove. Ctrl+C, --timeout or a runtime that goes away ends the command at once and leaves the reply running in the chat Live check: list-chats finds it, cancel <chatId> stops the reply and delete-chat <chatId> removes the chat.

options.name: provider
options.description: The id of the provider to check.

options.name: prompt
options.default: Reply with the single word PONG and do nothing else.

examples.description: Checks provider a1, giving it two minutes.

commands.name: teamrun.listTeammates
commands.description: Prints each teammate's id, name, harness, provider with its email, model and effort, the chats it is in, and whether it is answering now, then its role, its last reply's usage in each chat and its provider's plan use. The JSON gives the same fields, leaving out the figures a provider doesn't report, and never a credential or the profile folder.
